answer: An attacker farming fake agents across an orchard of accounts, a dune of wallets, or a meadow of fresh keys must fund every bond, so the cost scales linearly with fake identity count while legitimate single agents pay once. Sybil resistance via stake-bonded identity: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, slashable if peers detect duplicate identities. This makes mass sybil creation economically irrational. From once0005's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
